The **2024 FIA Formula One World Championship** was a motor racing championship for [Formula One cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_cars "Formula One cars") and was the 75th running of the [Formula One World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_World_Championship "Formula One World Championship"). It was recognised by the [Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F%C3%A9d%C3%A9ration_Internationale_de_l'Automobile "Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile") (FIA), the governing body of international [motorsport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motorsport "Motorsport"), as the highest class of competition for [open-wheel racing cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-wheel_racing_car "Open-wheel racing car"). The championship was contested over a record twenty-four [Grands Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One#Grands_Prix "Formula One") held around the world.
Drivers and teams competed for the titles of [World Drivers' Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_World_Drivers'_Champions "List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions") and [World Constructors' Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Formula_One_World_Constructors'_Champions "List of Formula One World Constructors' Champions") respectively. Defending world drivers’ champion [Max Verstappen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen "Max Verstappen") of [Red Bull Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing") dominated the opening 10 races with seven wins; however, the season as a whole was highly competitive, with a record-breaking six other drivers claiming multiple Grand Prix victories. [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren") driver [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris") emerged as Verstappen's closest competitor, as the [MCL38](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_MCL38 "McLaren MCL38") began to consistently outperform the [RB20](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing_RB20 "Red Bull Racing RB20"), Verstappen outscored Norris by 69 points across the opening 10 rounds, across the final 14 Norris would outscore Verstappen, with Verstappen failing to win from rounds 11 to 20. Verstappen maintained his points advantage to win his fourth consecutive Drivers' Championship title at the [Las Vegas Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Las_Vegas_Grand_Prix "2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix"). Verstappen's title made him the third drivers' champion after [Keke Rosberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keke_Rosberg "Keke Rosberg") in [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Formula_One_World_Championship "1982 Formula One World Championship") and [Nelson Piquet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_Piquet "Nelson Piquet") in [1983](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1983_Formula_One_World_Championship "1983 Formula One World Championship") to win the drivers' championship with a team that finished 3rd or lower in the constructors' championship. McLaren surpassed Red Bull and went on to achieve their ninth Constructors' Championship title at the [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix"), narrowly ahead of [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") by just 14 points. With their first Constructors' Championship victory [in 26 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_Formula_One_World_Championship "1998 Formula One World Championship"), McLaren became the first constructor other than Red Bull and [Mercedes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One") to win the title since [Brawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brawn_GP "Brawn GP") in 2009.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Free practice drivers")]
Throughout the season, each team had to field a driver in one of the first two free practice sessions who had not competed in more than two races, on two occasions, once for each car.[[2.2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-38) [Oliver Bearman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Bearman "Oliver Bearman")'s debut for [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") at the [Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix") did not count, as he only participated in the third practice session. ### Team changes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Team changes")]
[Alfa Romeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfa_Romeo_in_Formula_One "Alfa Romeo in Formula One") ended their partnership with [Sauber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauber_Motorsport "Sauber Motorsport") and left Formula One following the conclusion of the [2023 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship") as Sauber prepared to become the [Audi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audi "Audi") works team from 2026.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Alfa_Romeo-40)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-41) The team was rebranded as [Stake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stake.com "Stake.com") F1 Team [Kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick_\(service\) "Kick \(service\)") Sauber, competing with the constructor name Kick Sauber.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-StakeRenamed-17)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-42) [AlphaTauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_AlphaTauri "Scuderia AlphaTauri") rebranded as [RB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB_Formula_One_Team "RB Formula One Team") and relocated the aerodynamics operations of the team to [Milton Keynes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milton_Keynes "Milton Keynes") in the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom") amidst a management restructure.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-AT_Rebrand_2024-26)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-AlphaTauri-43)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-44)

[Liam Lawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Lawson "Liam Lawson") (center left) replaced [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") (center right) from the [United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_Grand_Prix "2024 United States Grand Prix") onwards. [Jack Doohan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Doohan "Jack Doohan") (bottom left) replaced [Esteban Ocon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esteban_Ocon "Esteban Ocon") (bottom right) at [Alpine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpine_F1_Team "Alpine F1 Team") at the [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix").
The only change from the drivers contracted at the beginning of [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship") occurred at the former [AlphaTauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_AlphaTauri "Scuderia AlphaTauri") team, who replaced [Nyck de Vries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nyck_de_Vries "Nyck de Vries") with [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") from the [2023 Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2023 Hungarian Grand Prix") onwards. All driver and team combinations that competed in the final round of the previous season remained unchanged for the start of the next season for the first time in Formula One World Championship history.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-45)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-46)
#### In-season changes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: In-season changes")]
[Carlos Sainz Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sainz_Jr. "Carlos Sainz Jr.") was forced to withdraw from the [Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix") after he was diagnosed with [appendicitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendicitis "Appendicitis") and required an [appendicectomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendicectomy "Appendicectomy").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-47) He was replaced by [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") reserve and [Formula 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIA_Formula_2_Championship "FIA Formula 2 Championship") driver [Oliver Bearman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Bearman "Oliver Bearman"), who made his Formula One debut.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:2-10) Sainz returned at the following [Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Australian_Grand_Prix "2024 Australian Grand Prix").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-APAussie-48) [Kevin Magnussen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Magnussen "Kevin Magnussen") of [Haas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haas_F1_Team "Haas F1 Team") received two penalty points for causing a collision at the Italian Grand Prix, taking his total to twelve penalty points in twelve months, and triggering an automatic race ban for the following [Azerbaijan Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2024 Azerbaijan Grand Prix").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:3-49) He was replaced by Bearman, who raced for the second time in the season as a reserve driver.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-50) Magnussen returned at the subsequent [Singapore Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2024 Singapore Grand Prix").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:3-49) Bearman replaced Magnussen at Haas again during the [São Paulo Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_S%C3%A3o_Paulo_Grand_Prix "2024 São Paulo Grand Prix") for the free practice and sprint sessions as Magnussen felt unwell.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-51)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-52)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-53) This was later expanded to the rest of the weekend following sprint qualifying.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Magnussen_out-15)
From the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Italian_Grand_Prix "2024 Italian Grand Prix") onwards, Formula 2 driver [Franco Colapinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Colapinto "Franco Colapinto") replaced [Logan Sargeant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_Sargeant "Logan Sargeant") at [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering "Williams Grand Prix Engineering"), making his Formula One debut. Sargeant was replaced following a series of poor performances, with team principal [James Vowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Vowles "James Vowles") stating that the driver change would give the team the best chance to score points over the remaining rounds.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Colapinto-54) [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") was dropped from [RB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RB_Formula_One_Team "RB Formula One Team") due to poor performance ahead of the [United States Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_Grand_Prix "2024 United States Grand Prix") with [Helmut Marko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helmut_Marko "Helmut Marko"), head of the [Red Bull's driver development programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Junior_Team "Red Bull Junior Team"), stating that Ricciardo had lost his "killer instinct".[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-55)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-56) He was replaced by the reserve driver [Liam Lawson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Lawson "Liam Lawson"), who drove in the [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship") season in place of the injured Ricciardo at the same team, then known as [AlphaTauri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_AlphaTauri "Scuderia AlphaTauri").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-LawsonIn-57) Reserve driver [Jack Doohan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Doohan "Jack Doohan") made his debut at the [Abu Dhabi Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Abu_Dhabi_Grand_Prix "2024 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix"), where he replaced [Esteban The [Chinese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Grand_Prix "Chinese Grand Prix") returned to the calendar for the first time since [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Formula_One_World_Championship "2019 Formula One World Championship") after being cancelled for four years in a row due to difficulties presented by the [COVID-19 pandemic in the country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_mainland_China "COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-63) The [Emilia Romagna Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix "Emilia Romagna Grand Prix"), which was [cancelled in the preceding year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix#Rain,_floods_and_subsequent_cancellation "2023 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix") due to [flooding in the area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Emilia-Romagna_floods "2023 Emilia-Romagna floods"), also returned to the calendar.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-64) The [Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Grand_Prix "Japanese Grand Prix") moved from its traditional October autumn date to one in April as part of the efforts to group races in regional blocks to help address environmental concerns surrounding travel between races. As a consequence the [Azerbaijan Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "Azerbaijan Grand Prix") moved from April to September.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-2024_calendar-59) The [Russian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Grand_Prix "Russian Grand Prix") was under contract to feature on the 2024 calendar,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-65) however the contract was terminated in [2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Formula_One_World_Championship "2022 Formula One World Championship") in response to the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-66)
## Regulation changes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Regulation changes")]
### Technical regulations
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Technical regulations")]
In response to extreme weather conditions resulting in cockpit overheating during the [2023 Qatar Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Qatar_Grand_Prix "2023 Qatar Grand Prix"), teams were now allowed to install a "scoop" to the car that is intended to cool down the driver and cockpit area.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:1-67) Teams were not allowed to start wind tunnel or [computational fluid dynamics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_fluid_dynamics "Computational fluid dynamics") work for the 2026 season, which will see major technical regulations rule changes, until 1 January 2025. However, teams were still allowed to do other preliminary research and development work not covered by these restrictions.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-68)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-69)
#### Tyres
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Tyres")]
The "alternative tyre allocation" trialled at the [2023 Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2023 Hungarian Grand Prix") and [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Italian_Grand_Prix "2023 Italian Grand Prix") Grands Prix, where drivers were given 11 sets of tyres in an attempt to cut costs in the sport, was discontinued. Therefore, teams reverted to having 13 sets of tyres available per driver during every non-sprint race weekend with the allocation being 12 sets for a sprint weekend.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-70) The C0 tyre compound (the hardest compound in [Pirelli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pirelli "Pirelli")'s dry tyre range), which was introduced but not used during the [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship") season, was dropped from the tyre line-up.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-Opening3Tyres-71) This compound was previously known as the C1, but was renamed at the start of the 2023 season following the introduction of a new C1 compound that slotted between the old C1 and current C2 compounds in terms of hardness.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-72) A proposed trial for a ban on tyre blankets for this season and a full ban in 2025 was abandoned.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:1-67)
### Sporting regulations
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Sporting regulations")]
#### Appeals process
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Appeals process")]
The decision appeal process was amended for the 2024 season. The deadline to submit a right of review request was reduced from fourteen to four days after an event. In an attempt to stop potentially frivolous appeal attempts, the FIA also introduced a fee for the process.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-TightenUpRoR-73)
#### Sprint weekend structure
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sprint weekend structure")]
The structure of the sprint weekends was changed again for 2024, with the goal of rationalising sprint events and separating them from the rest of the Grand Prix weekend.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-74)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:1-67) A sprint weekend began with a single practice session, followed by the sprint qualifying session, which set the starting grid order for the sprint race. The sprint was then the first session to take place on Saturday, followed by qualifying for the main race. The Grand Prix itself remained on Sunday.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-75) The FIA sporting regulations for the championship now referred to the qualifying for the sprint as "sprint qualifying", as opposed to "sprint shootout". The term "sprint qualifying" was previously used in the inaugural season of the sprint format in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Formula_One_World_Championship "2021 Formula One World Championship") to refer to the sprint itself.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-76) Additionally, sprint weekends now had two separate [parc fermé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parc_ferm%C3%A9 "Parc fermé") periods as opposed to one. The first lasted from the beginning of sprint qualifying to the end of the sprint, and the second lasted from the beginning of qualifying for the Grand Prix until the start of the Grand Prix itself.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-77)
#### DRS usage
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: DRS usage")]
The rules for [DRS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drag_reduction_system "Drag reduction system") usage in Grands Prix were adjusted slightly. Drivers were now allowed to use DRS one lap after a race start, safety car restart, or red flag restart, one lap earlier than in previous seasons. This modification, tested during sprint events in 2023, was implemented to encourage earlier overtaking opportunities and increase competitiveness in the opening stages of a race.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:4-78)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-79)
#### Power unit allocation
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Power unit allocation")]
The FIA increased the number of internal combustion engine (ICE) components and associated power unit elements allowed per driver from three to four per season. This change was made to accommodate the record-length calendar and reduce the frequency of grid penalties caused by engine wear and failure.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:4-78)
#### Maximum lap time
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Maximum lap time")]
Prior to Thursday's two practice sessions at the season-opening [Bahrain Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2024 Bahrain Grand Prix"), updated rules were introduced to discourage drivers from driving too slowly on in-laps and reconnaissance laps during qualifying. Drivers were initially required to not exceed a maximum time taken to drive through each marshalling sector. This was a change from 2023, when the FIA introduced a maximum time across an entire lap.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-80) However, prior to Friday's third practice session and qualifying, the rules were reverted to the 2023 full-lap method, though the rule now applied on both in-laps and out-laps.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-81)
#### Penalties
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Penalties")]
The standard sanction for a driver overtaking another driver off the track and gaining a lasting advantage was upgraded from a five-second time penalty to a ten-second time penalty, although five-second penalties could still be awarded. The change was made as the five-second penalty was considered insufficient, with drivers regularly gaining more than five seconds through illegally overtaking slower cars off track.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-82)
From the [Miami Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Miami_Grand_Prix "2024 Miami Grand Prix") onwards the FIA altered the regulations for judging a potential [jump start](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jump_start_\(motorsport\) "Jump start \(motorsport\)"). Under the previous regulations, stewards were unable to penalise a driver for a jump start if it had not been picked up by an FIA [transponder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transponder#Motorsport "Transponder"). This rule led to [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris") of [McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren") appearing to avoid a penalty despite visibly moving early at the start of the [Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix"). The update to regulations allowed stewards to penalise a driver if they were moving before the start, even if the transponder did not register the infringement. The regulation also clarified jump starts would be judged "after the four-second light is illuminated and before the start signal is given by extinguishing all red lights."[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-RFJumpStarts-83)
From the [Dutch Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dutch_Grand_Prix "2024 Dutch Grand Prix"), penalties accrued during the sprint race which could not be served, due to retirement, could be transferred into grid penalties for their next race. This had already been the case for penalties accrued in Grands Prix.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:0-84)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-MidSeasonPF1-85)
#### Testing
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Testing")]
During the summer break, the regulations were updated to allow teams to create [mule cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Development_mule "Development mule") based on existing cars from the [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Formula_One_World_Championship "2020 Formula One World Championship")–[2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Formula_One_World_Championship "2023 Formula One World Championship") period to enable teams to better prepare for the changes to the technical regulations due for the [2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Formula_One_World_Championship "2026 Formula One World Championship") season. Teams using the mule cars would only be allowed to use drivers with 500 kilometres (310 mi) of experience of driving a current Formula One car at consistent racing speeds.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-MidSeasonPF1-85)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-86)
#### Red flag procedure
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Red flag procedure")]
During the summer break, the regulations for red flag procedures were clarified: during a red flag period, cars could be instructed to line-up on the starting grid, instead of in the pit lane, where the pit lane needed to be closed for safety reasons. The regulations were additionally altered to state that a driver who stops outside of the pit lane during qualifying and receives physical assistance will no longer be able to participate in qualifying.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:0-84)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-MidSeasonPF1-85)
## Season summary
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Season summary")]
### Pre-season
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Pre-season")]
A single pre-season test was held at the [Bahrain International Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bahrain_International_Circuit "Bahrain International Circuit") in [Sakhir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakhir "Sakhir") on 21–23 February.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-87)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-88) [Carlos Sainz Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Sainz_Jr. "Carlos Sainz Jr.") of [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") set the fastest time in the three-day test, [Haas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haas_F1_Team "Haas F1 Team") completed the most laps.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-89)
### Opening rounds
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Opening rounds")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Verstappen_%26_Perez_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg/250px-Verstappen_%26_Perez_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Verstappen_&_Perez_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg)[Red Bull Racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Bull_Racing "Red Bull Racing") dominated the opening races of the season with 1–2 victories at the [Bahrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2024 Bahrain Grand Prix"), [Saudi Arabian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix") and [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2024 Japanese Grand Prix") Grands Prix, and a 1–3 at the [Chinese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Chinese_Grand_Prix "2024 Chinese Grand Prix").
[Max Verstappen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Verstappen "Max Verstappen") took pole position at the season opening [2024 Bahrain Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Bahrain_Grand_Prix "2024 Bahrain Grand Prix") ahead of [Charles Leclerc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Leclerc "Charles Leclerc") and [George Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Russell_\(racing_driver\) "George Russell \(racing driver\)"). Verstappen's teammate, and 2023 Championship runner-up, [Sergio Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_P%C3%A9rez "Sergio Pérez") qualified fifth.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-90) The top three all held their positions at the race start, with Perez moving into fourth ahead of Sainz. Leclerc would lose positions to both Russell, Perez and Sainz in the opening laps. Through the opening pit stops, Perez overtook Russell on track and Leclerc regained a position on Sainz by exucuting an [undercut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undercut_\(motorsport\) "Undercut \(motorsport\)"); Sainz would soon make his way back past and would also pass Russell shortly afterwards - although Russell was suffering technical issues - Russell would drop behind Leclerc before the race end. The top five would hold their positions to the race end, with Norris coming in sixth.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-BensonBahrain-91)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-92)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-93) Following the race, Verstappen led the Drivers' Championship by 8 points from Pérez and 11 from Sainz, eventual championship runnerup Norris was in 6th, 18 points behind Verstappen. In the Constructors' Standings, defending champions Red Bull led [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") by 17 points, [Mercedes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_in_Formula_One "Mercedes-Benz in Formula One") were an additional 11 points back in third and McLaren were 4th, 32 points behind Red Bull.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-94)
At the [Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix"), Verstappen took pole.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-95) Verstappen led the opening laps of the race. A [safety car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_car "Safety car") period, following a crash involving [Lance Stroll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Stroll "Lance Stroll"), was called on lap 7. Verstappen, along with the top 5, chose to make a pitstop during this phase, with Norris inheriting the lead. Verstappen overtook Norris for the lead on lap 12, and held it for the rest of the race. Pérez finished second, having started in third, making his way past Leclerc for second in the early stages, Leclerc maintained third to the race's conclusion. [Oscar Piastri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Piastri "Oscar Piastri") finished fourth, having struggled to overtake [Lewis Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton "Lewis Hamilton") for a large portion of the race. During the weekend, Sainz was affected with [appendicitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendicitis "Appendicitis"), which resulted in his withdrawal from the event on Friday morning to have surgery. In his place, [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") junior driver [Oliver Bearman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Bearman "Oliver Bearman"), stood in for Sainz.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-96) Bearman qualified eleventh and went on to finish seventh, and was widely praised for his performance, having missed the weekend's opening two practice sessions.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-97) Following the races' conclusion, Verstappen extended his championship lead to 15 points over Pérez, Leclerc moved into third, 12 points further behind. Norris was seventh, 39 points behind Verstappen. Red Bull extended their lead to 38 points over Ferrari, McLaren moved into third, an additional 21 points behind.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-98)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-:5-99)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-100)
Alex Albon crashed his car heavily during the first practice session for the Australian Grand Prix, writing off the chassis. With no spare chassis available, Williams made the decision for Albon to take over Logan Sargeant's car, with Sargeant withdrawing from the weekend. Team principal James Vowles justified this decision by arguing Albon had a better chance to score points, and praised Sargeant for his sportsmanship.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-AlbonSwap-35) Verstappen took pole position, with Sainz second and Pérez qualifying third,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-101) Pérez was demoted three places for impeding, promoting Norris to third on the starting grid.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-102) Verstappen retained the lead at the race start, before suffering from brake issues, Sainz made his way past Verstappen into the lead on lap 2, with Verstappen retiring the car shortly afterwards. This retirement meant Verstappen would fail to take a record equalling 10th consecutive victory. Sainz was able to build a lead over his rivals and secured the win largely unchalleged. His teammate [Charles Leclerc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Leclerc "Charles Leclerc") successfully [undercut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undercut_\(motorsport\) "Undercut \(motorsport\)") Norris to take second. Norris completed the podium and succeeded [Nick Heidfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Heidfeld "Nick Heidfeld") for the most podiums without a victory in Formula One. Piastri finished fourth, having been instructed to let Norris, with Pérez fifth. Alonso and Russell were running sixth and seventh in the final stages, with Russell attacking Alonso, before Russell crashed in the closing laps, Alonso was deemed to have driven in a "potentially dangerous way in the build up to the incident earning him a post race penalty.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-103) Following the race Verstappen and Red Bull maintained their championship leads with 51 and 97 points respectively. In the drivers' championship Leclerc moved to second, on 47 points with Pérez third on 46, Norris was 6th on 27. In the constructors', Ferrari closed the gap to 4 points, with McLaren 42 points behind Red Bull.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-104)
Verstappen took pole position at the [Japanese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2024 Japanese Grand Prix"), 0.066 seconds ahead of Pérez, who had his first front-row start since the [2023 Miami Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Miami_Grand_Prix "2023 Miami Grand Prix"), with Norris third and Sainz fourth.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-105) The top five maintained their positions at the race start, before the race was red-flagged due to a heavy crash that involved [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") and [Alexander Albon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Albon "Alexander Albon") at turn three, which necessitated repairs to the tyre barriers. The top runners again maintained position at the restart, with Verstappen quickly managing to extend a one-second lead, putting him outside DRS range. Norris was the first on the front runners to pit on lap 12, with the rest of the top four following suit over the next few laps, with Norris [undercutting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undercut_\(motorsport\) "Undercut \(motorsport\)") Pérez and Leclerc taking the lead, having yet to make a stop, over the following laps, Verstappen retook the race lead, and Pérez regained second from both Norris and Leclerc before the latter made his pitstop, undercutting Norris into third. In the closing stages Sainz closed in on and overtook Norris for fourth, and then overtook teammate Leclerc for third courtesy of team orders, Sainz was the faster car and [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari "Scuderia Ferrari") felt that a battle for position would risk Norris catching and overtaking at least one of the pair. The race therefore ended with Verstappen winning ahead of Pérez, Sainz and Leclerc with Norris in fifth.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-106)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-107)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-108) Ricciardo's teammate Tsunoda scored a point, making him the first [Japanese driver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_drivers_from_Japan "Formula One drivers from Japan") to score points at their home race since [Kamui Kobayashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamui_Kobayashi "Kamui Kobayashi")'s podium in the [2012 edition of the race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Japanese_Grand_Prix "2012 Japanese Grand Prix").[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-109) Following the race, Verstappen extended his Championship lead to 13 points, with Pérez moving into second, Leclerc a further four points back on 59. Sainz remained in fourth with Norris moving up to fifth. In the constructors' Championship, Red Bull moved to 141 points, 21 ahead of Ferrari and 72 ahead of McLaren.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-110)
The [Chinese Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Chinese_Grand_Prix "2024 Chinese Grand Prix") saw the first sprint of the season. Sprint qualifying was held in wet conditions and ended with Norris taking pole ahead of Hamilton and Fernando Alonso.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-111) Championship leader Verstappen struggled in the first [sprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_sprint "Formula One sprint") qualifying of the season, ending up fourth.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-112) Verstappen went on to win the sprint race, he gained one position at the first turn, after polesitter Norris ran wide and dropped to seventh after the first lap. Verstappen overtook Alonso for second on lap 7, and Hamilton for the lead on lap 9 where he remained for the rest of the race. Behind Verstappen, Hamilton finished second. In the closing laps, a fight for third place emerged between Alonso, Pérez, Leclerc, Sainz and Norris. Sainz attempted an overtake on Alonso, opening a gap for Pérez to take third and Leclerc fourth. Alonso dropped back with a puncture, allowing Sainz to take fifth ahead of Norris.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-113) Verstappen took Red Bull's 100th pole position for the Grand Prix, ahead of Pérez and Alonso.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-114) Verstappen managed to maintain his lead into the opening turn, while Alonso managed to overtake Pérez for second around the outside of turn 1. Norris and Piastri retained fourth and fifth. The Ferrari pair of Leclerc and Sainz dropped to seventh and eighth. The opening laps saw Alonso drop down to fourth behind Pérez and Norris, and Leclerc move up to fifth, gaining positions from Hülkenberg, Russell and Piastri before the pit stop phase opened. Alonso, Verstappen, Pérez, Piastri and Sainz all made pit stops before a [safety car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_car "Safety car") was deployed. Under this safety car, Norris and Leclerc made their only pitstops of the race, with Verstappen, Pérez and Piastri taking second pit stops for fresher tyres. This saw Verstappen leading from Norris, Leclerc, Pérez and Sainz, Russell, Leclerc and Piastri. The second half of the race saw a battle develop between Leclerc and Pérez for the final podium position, with Pérez moving into third on lap 39. Verstappen was able to win the race, ahead of Norris, Pérez, Leclerc, Sainz, Russell, Alonso and Piastri.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-115)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-116) At the races conclusion, Verstappen moved to 110 points, 25 clear of Pérez in second, and 34 clear of Leclerc in third. Sainz and Leclerc retained fourth and fifth on 69 and 58 points. In the Constructors' standings, Red Bull moved 44 points clear of second placed Ferrari, with McLaren a further 55 points back.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-117)
The [Miami Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Miami_Grand_Prix "2024 Miami Grand Prix") saw a second consecutive sprint weekend. In sprint qualifying, Verstappen took pole from Leclerc and Pérez, with Sainz fifth behind Ricciardo.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-118) The Mclaren pair were fastest across practice and the opening sprint qualifying sessions but were unable to replicate this in the final part of sprint qualifying and ended up sixth and ninth.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-119) At the start of the sprint, Verstappen immediately covered the inside of the opening turn to maintain first place. Pérez attempted a move for second around the outside of the corner but ran wide, yielding third to [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo"). Norris was tipped into a spin at the first corner, and was then hit by Stroll, causing Norris' retirement with terminal damage. After a brief safety car period, the lead drivers initially maintained position. Ricciardo was overtaken for third on lap 5. The race ended with Verstappen winning from Leclerc and Pérez, with Ricciardo able to narrowly hold on to fourth from Sainz and Piastri.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-120) Verstappen took pole for the Grand Prix ahead of Leclerc, Sainz, Pérez and the McLaren duo of Norris and Piastri.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-121) Verstappen was able to maintain his lead through the first corner. Behind, Pérez locked his front tyres causing Sainz and Leclerc to take avoiding action. Leclerc was able to maintain second, with Piastri making his way up to third ahead of Sainz, Pérez and Norris. A couple of laps into the Grands Prix, Piastri was able to overtake Leclerc for second. Pérez was the first of leading cars to pit, and was soon followed by Leclerc, Verstappen, Piastri and Sainz before the safety car was deployed following a collision between Magnussen and Sargeant. Norris took advantage of this to make a pitstop and rejoined the track in first, ahead of Verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Sainz and Pérez. At the safety car restart, Verstappen briefly challeneged Norris for lead, before Norris was able to pull away. Sainz managed to make his way past Piastri. Piastri attempted to retake the position, but collided with Sainz, forcing Piastri to pit for repairs and dropping him out of the points. Norris took his maiden Formula One victory, having previously held the record of the most podiums without a victory, and giving McLaren their first victory since the [2021 Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Italian_Grand_Prix "2021 Italian Grand Prix"). Verstappen was second from Leclerc, Pérez, Sainz, with Hamilton achieving his best result of the season to that point with sixth. Ocon scored Alpine's first point of the season with tenth place.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-122) Following the event, Verstappen increased his points tally to 136, 33 ahead of second placed Pérez, with Leclerc in third an additional five points back and Sainz and Norris both on 83 points. In the Constructors Championship, Red Bull extended their lead over second placed Ferrari to 52, and their lead over third place McLaren to 115.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-123)
### Mid-season rounds
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Mid-season rounds")]
At the [Emilia Romagna Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Emilia_Romagna_Grand_Prix "2024 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix"), Verstappen took an "unexpected" pole by 0.074 seconds, equalling [Ayrton Senna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayrton_Senna "Ayrton Senna")'s record of eight consecutive pole positions.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-124) Piastri was second, ahead of Norris and the Ferrari pair of Leclerc and Sainz, Pérez qualified 11th.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-125) Piastri was demoted to fifth on the starting grid for impeding another driver during qualifying.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-126) The top six drivers held positions on the opening lap, with Pérez making up ground and overtaking [Daniel Ricciardo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo "Daniel Ricciardo") for tenth. The leading cars made their pit stops around the twenty lap mark with McLaren duo pitting first and then Verstappen, and the Ferrari pair. During the pit stop phase, Piastri was able to successfully [undercut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undercut_\(motorsport\) "Undercut \(motorsport\)") Sainz for fourth place. As the race reached the 40 lap mark, Leclerc closed the gap to Norris, Leclerc being told he was the faster driver of the pair. By lap 50, Norris had stronger pace and was able to pull away from Leclerc and was also able to start closing the gap forward to Verstappen. Norris closed within a couple of seconds of Verstappen, but was unable to overtake before the races conclusion. Verstappen therefore won the race, ahead of Norris and Leclerc. Piastri claimed fourth ahead of Sainz, Pérez recovered to 8th.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-127) Norris stated that he could have overtaken Verstappen if the race were a couple of laps longer.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-128) Following the race, Verstappen moved to 161 points in the Drivers Championship. Leclerc moved up to second on 113 with Pérez dropping to third on 107. Norris moved into a clear fourth, 6 points behind Pérez. In the Constructors' Standings, Red Bull's lead increased to 56 points over Ferrari, with McLaren a further 58 behind.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-129)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/2024-08-25_Motorsport%2C_Formel_1%2C_Gro%C3%9Fer_Preis_der_Niederlande_2024_STP_3919_by_Stepro.jpg/250px-2024-08-25_Motorsport%2C_Formel_1%2C_Gro%C3%9Fer_Preis_der_Niederlande_2024_STP_3919_by_Stepro.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2024-08-25_Motorsport,_Formel_1,_Gro%C3%9Fer_Preis_der_Niederlande_2024_STP_3919_by_Stepro.jpg)By winning the [Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Monaco_Grand_Prix "2024 Monaco Grand Prix"), [Charles Leclerc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Leclerc "Charles Leclerc") became only the second Monégasque driver after [Louis Chiron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Chiron "Louis Chiron") in [1931](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1931_Monaco_Grand_Prix "1931 Monaco Grand Prix") to win at their home Grand Prix.
Verstappen's record equaling run of consecutive pole positions ended at the [Monaco Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Monaco_Grand_Prix "2024 Monaco Grand Prix"), as he qualified sixth. Pole position was instead taken by Monégasque Leclerc, ahead of Piastri, Sainz and Norris, Pérez qualified 18th.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-130) At the start Leclerc held position, Piastri and Sainz collided lightly at the first corner, resulting in Sainz receiving a puncture which dropped him down the field. Pérez, Magnussen and Hulkenberg were also involved in a collision which stranded the three cars on track, causing a [red flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racing_flags#Red_flag "Racing flags"). The race was restarted based on the original starting order, meaning that Sainz would retain his third place start. For the second start, the drivers changed tyre compound, therefore fulfilling the rule to run two tyre compounds allowing them to complete the race without a pit stop. The race was run with the top five within a few seconds of each other, but no overtaking attempts. Leclerc took his first win since the [2022 Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2022 Austrian Grand Prix") and the first at his home Grand Prix. [Oscar Piastri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Piastri "Oscar Piastri") took his first podium of the season in second, and Sainz finished third.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-131) Following the race, Verstappen's championship lead over Lerclerc was cut to 31 points. Norris and Sainz moved up to third and fourth, 56 and 61 points behind Verstappen, respectively. Pérez dropped to fifth, one point behind Sainz. In the Constructors' Standings, Red Bull's lead was cut to 24 points over Ferrari, and 92 over McLaren.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-132)
After Verstappen and Russell set identical lap times during qualifying for the [Canadian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Canadian_Grand_Prix "2024 Canadian Grand Prix"), Russell secured pole position by virtue of setting the time first. Norris and Piastri were third and fourth, the Ferrari 11th and 12th with Pérez 16th.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-133) The race began under wet conditions. Most of the field elected to start the race on the [intermediate wet tyre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One_tyres#Tyre_summary "Formula One tyres"), with the Haas duo of Magnussen and Hülkenberg starting on the full wet tyre. The leading drivers held position on the opening laps. A band of heavy rain played into Haas' favour with Magnussen and Hülkenberg able to make their way through the field, with Magnussen running as high as fourth before the rain eased, and he lost his advantage. With the track starting to dry up, Norris was setting the fastest lap times and was able to make his way into the lead by 21. Verstappen also overtook Russell for second. Norris was able to pull away from Verstappen, with Russell dropping back towards Piastri. The safety car was deployed shortly afterwards, Verstappen and Russell made pit stops immediately, although Norris missed the pit lane and had to complete another lap. This allowed Verstappen and Russell to [undercut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undercut_\(motorsport\) "Undercut \(motorsport\)") Norris for first and second. After the safety car was withdrawn, Norris was once again the fastest car on track, but was unable to make a pass on Russell for second. Verstappen and Russell both made pitstops around lap 40 for dry weather tyres, with Norris electing to stay out until lap 47. When Norris made his stop, he was able to [overcut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overcut_\(motorsport\) "Overcut \(motorsport\)") Russell and rejoined the track side by side with Verstappen. Verstappen was able to take first, and Norris dropped back on colder tyres, being overtaken by Russell for second, before Rusell made an error, allowing Norris back through. The closing laps saw Verstappen and Norris pull clear and maintain first and second to the end. A fight ensued for the final podium position, which was claimed by Russell ahead of Hamilton and Piastri. Leclerc, Sainz and Pérez all retired.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-134) The result saw Verstappen maintain the lead (on 194 points) ahead of Leclerc (138), Norris (131). In the Constructors, Red Bull moved to 301 points, ahead of Ferrari (252) and McLaren (212).[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-135)
Norris took his second career pole position at the [Spanish Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Spanish_Grand_Prix "2024 Spanish Grand Prix"), ahead of Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Leclerc and Sainz. Pérez started the race in eleventh.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-136) At the start, Norris moved across the track to cut off Verstappen, with Verstappen ending up in the grass Russell was able to go around the outside of both of them at turn one and took the race lead and Verstappen moving up into second. Lap three saw Verstappen take the lead from Russell. The top three retained their positions until lap 16 when Russell made his pit stop, with Verstappen pitting on lap 17 and Norris on lap 24, with the order staying the same amongst the top three after the initial pit stop phase. Verstappen was able to extend his lead to eight seconds over Russell and Norris, who were fighting for second place, with Norris able to claim the position on lap 35; Russell and Norris's fight allowed Verstappen to extend his lead to nine seconds by the end of lap 36. Norris was able to start eating into Verstappen's lead after taking second, with Norris closing the gap to four seconds by the time Verstappen made his second pit stop on lap 46; this saw Verstappen able to lap faster than Norris. Norris made his own pit stop a few laps later; but it was a slow one, and Norris rejoined the race just ahead of Russell and seven seconds back from Verstappen. Over the closing laps, Norris ate into Verstappen's lead, but was unable to get close eough to attempt an overtake. Verstappen therefore won by 2.2 seconds from Norris; with Hamilton claiming third after overtaking Russell in the closing stages. Russell finished ahead of Leclerc and Sainz.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-137)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-138) The result saw Verstappen extend his championship lead to 69 points, with Norris moving into second ahead of Leclerc. In the constructor's championship, Red Bull's lead increased to 60 points over Ferrari, with McLaren a further 33 back.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-139)
The [Austrian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Austrian_Grand_Prix "2024 Austrian Grand Prix") featured the third sprint of the season. Verstappen took pole for the sprint race, ahead of Norris and Piastri. Leclerc, third in the drivers championship suffered mechanical problems which left him tenth.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-140) In the sprint, Verstappen, Norris and Piastri maintained positions through the opening laps, although Norris did have to defend an overtaking attempt from Piastri on the opening lap, going into turn three. On lap 5, Norris overtook Verstappen going into turn three, before Verstappen retook the position at turn four. Verstappen's overtake left Norris compromised on the corner exit and allowed Piastri to move into second. From there Verstappen was able to successfully pull away, Norris was able to close the gap and apply pressure to Piastri but did not attempt a serious overtaking manoeuvre. Verstappen therefore won the sprint from Piastri and Norris, with Leclerc seventh.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-141) Verstappen also took pole position for the main race, ahead of Norris, Russell and Sainz. Leclerc and Piastri were sixth and seventh, with both of them having off track excursions at the end of the session.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-142) At the race start, the top three maintained their positions. Leclerc and Piastri made contact at the first turn; Leclerc suffered front wing damage and he made a pitstop for repairs. The opening laps saw Verstappen, Norris and Russell maintain positions, with the gap between the three of them consistently increasing. The leading trio all made their first pit stop between laps 23 and 24 and maintaining their relative positions, with Sainz fourth, Hamilton fifth and Piastri sixth. On lap 52, Norris and Verstappen both made their second pit stops on lap 52. Verstappen suffered a slow pit stop, which allowed Norris to close the gap to around two seconds, down from seven on lap 49. Norris was able to close the gap further and made several overtaking attempts over the following laps. On lap 64, when Norris attempted another overtaking attempt, Norris and Verstappen made contact. Norris retired the car, and Verstappen suffered a puncture which dropped him to fifth; Verstappen was penalised for the collision. The collision allowed Russell to move into the lead ahead of Piastri (who overtook Hamilton on lap 47 and Sainz on lap 55) and Sainz. The race was won by Russell, the second of his career, ahead of Piastri, Sainz, Hamilton and Verstappen.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-143)[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-144) Following the race's conclusion, Verstappen extended his championship lead to 81 points over Norris and 87 points over Leclerc. Red Bull extended their championship lead to 64 points over Ferrari. McLaren (in third) closed the gap to Ferrari to 23 points.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-145)
Russell took pole position for the [British Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_British_Grand_Prix "2024 British Grand Prix"), ahead of Hamilton, Norris, Verstappen and Piastri.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-146) The opening laps saw Russell and Hamilton maintain position and pull away from Verstappen who had moved into third. Norris was able to successfully move back into third on lap 13 with rain starting to fall at around the same time. Piastri overtook Verstappen for fourth shortly afterwards. The following laps saw the McLaren's of Norris and Piastri close the gap to the Mercedes duo. Hamilton overtook Russell on lap 18. By lap 20, both McLaren's had overtaken both Mercedes (Hamilton and Russell) to make the top five: Norris, Piastri, Hamilton, Russell. Of the leaders, Verstappen made the first pit stop on lap 27, followed by Norris, Hamilton and Russell on lap 28 and Piastri on lap 29, all changing to the [intermediate-wet tyres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermediate_tyres "Intermediate tyres"). Following the opening pit stops, Verstappen was able to [undercut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undercut_\(motorsport\) "Undercut \(motorsport\)") Russell for third, and Piatri dropped to sixth. Russell retired with a water leak shortly afterwards. Hamilton, Verstappen and Piastri all made pit stops on lap 39. Norris suffered a slow stop on lap 40. This moved Hamilton into the lead ahead of Norris, Verstappen and Piastri. The closing laps saw Verstappen close the gap to Norris and successfully overtake him, before beginning to chase down Hamilton, although he would end up short. Hamilton therefore took the win, his first since the [2021 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Saudi_Arabian_Grand_Prix "2021 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix"), ahead of Verstappen and Norris with Piastri fourth.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-147)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-148) Following the race, Verstappen moved to 255 championship points, with Norris second (171) and Leclerc third (150). In the Constructors, Red Bull's championship lead increased to 71 points over Ferrari. McLaren, in third, closed the gap to both Ferrari (7 points) and Red Bull (78 points).[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-149)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Norris_%26_Piastri_on_the_grid_-_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg/250px-Norris_%26_Piastri_on_the_grid_-_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Norris_&_Piastri_on_the_grid_-_Chinese_GP_2024.jpg)[McLaren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren "McLaren") drivers [Lando Norris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lando_Norris "Lando Norris") (left) and [Oscar Piastri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oscar_Piastri "Oscar Piastri") (right) claimed their maiden wins at the [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Miami_Grand_Prix "2024 Miami Grand Prix") and [Hungarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2024 Hungarian Grand Prix") Grands Prix, respectively.
Norris and Piastri took first and second in qualifying for the [Hungarian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Hungarian_Grand_Prix "2024 Hungarian Grand Prix"), McLaren's first front-row lockout since the [2012 Brazilian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Brazilian_Grand_Prix "2012 Brazilian Grand Prix"). Verstappen qualified third ahead of Sainz, Hamilton and Leclerc.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-150) Norris, Piastri and Verstappen went three wide at the race start, with Piastri coming out on top. Verstappen went wide off the track, and went into second ahead of Norris. Verstappen was instructed by Red Bull to let Norris back past into second, Hamilton was fourth and Leclerc fifth. The top five maintained their positions into the first pit stop phase. Hamilton was the first of the leading five to make his pit stop, followed on consecutive laps by Norris and Piastri, with Verstappen making his stop 5 laps after Hamilton. Piastri and Norris remained in net first and second, but Hamilton successfully [undercut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undercut_\(motorsport\) "Undercut \(motorsport\)") Verstappen into third. The leaders maintained their positions through the next stint; with Hamilton defending several overtake attempts from Verstappen. Hamilton and Leclerc both made their second pit stops on 41, followed by Norris on lap 46, Piastri on lap 48 and Verstappen on lap 50. Through the second pit stops, Leclerc was able to undercut Verstappen and Norris undercut Piastri. Norris was immediately told to "reestablish the order at your convenience" an instruction to let Piastri back into the lead. A few laps later, McLaren told Piastri that Norris would let him past "once you get to Lando [Norris]" - the gap at the time was three seconds. Over the following laps, McLaren gave several instructions over team radio to Norris instructing him to allow Piastri into the lead. The McLaren's swapped positions on lap 68 of 70. Verstappen made it past Leclerc, he then fought Hamilton for third. Verstappen made several attempts for the position. On one of these he went off track and lost fourth to Leclerc. Piastri therefore won the race, his first Formula One win, ahead of Norris, Hamilton, Leclerc and Verstappen.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-151)[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-152) Following the race, McLaren team principal [Andrea Stella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrea_Stella "Andrea Stella") confirmed that swapping positions was an agreed action if one driver had gained over the other during the pitstop phase.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-153) Following the race, Verstappen's championship lead was reduced to 76 points from Norris, Norris's advantage over Leclerc in third increased to 27. Red Bull remained in the lead of the constructors's championship, on 389. McLaren moved into second in the championship on 338 points, with Ferrari in third on 322.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-154)
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/2024-08-24_Motorsport%2C_Formel_1%2C_Gro%C3%9Fer_Preis_der_Niederlande_2024_STP_3368_by_Stepro.jpg/250px-2024-08-24_Motorsport%2C_Formel_1%2C_Gro%C3%9Fer_Preis_der_Niederlande_2024_STP_3368_by_Stepro.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2024-08-24_Motorsport,_Formel_1,_Gro%C3%9Fer_Preis_der_Niederlande_2024_STP_3368_by_Stepro.jpg)At the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2024 Belgian Grand Prix"), [George Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Russell_\(racing_driver\) "George Russell \(racing driver\)") became the first driver to be disqualified from a Grand Prix victory since [Michael Schumacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Schumacher "Michael Schumacher") in the [1994 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Belgian_Grand_Prix "1994 Belgian Grand Prix") of the race.
Verstappen qualified fastest for the [Belgian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Belgian_Grand_Prix "2024 Belgian Grand Prix"), before a penalty for taking too many engine components dropped him to 11th. This promoted Leclerc to pole positions, ahead of Pérez, Hamilton, Norris, Piastri and Russell.[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-155) Leclerc successfully held the lead at the start, with Hamilton making his way past Pérez. Hamilton would take the lead from Leclerc two laps later. Norris ran wide at the first corner, dropping to seventh, with Verstappen eighth at the end of lap two. The leaders made their first pit stops from lap 14. During this phase, Russell undercut Piastri, and Verstappen undercut Norris. Piastri would overtake Russell and Perez in quick succession to move into net third. Perez would also lose a position to Russell before making his second pit stop on lap 21. The other leading drivers, apart from Russell, made their second pit stops between laps 26 and 31. This left Russell in the lead, approximately six seconds ahead of Hamilton in second, being followed by Leclerc, Piastri, Verstappen, Norris, Pérez and Sainz. Over the following laps, Piastri made several attempts for third from Leclerc before successfully taking the position. By lap 40 of 44, Hamilton had closed the gap to within one second of Russell and started to look for an overtaking opportunity. Hamilton made several attempts but was unsuccessful. Russell was therefore able to cross the finish line in first, having made one stop fewer than his rivals. Russell was later disqualified for having an underweight car. Hamilton therefore inherited the race win, ahead of Piastri and Leclerc, with Verstappen fourth and Norris fifth.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-BelgianGP-156)[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-157) Following the Grand Prix, Versappen's championship lead increased to 78 over Norris. Leclerc moved to 22 points behind Norris. In the constructors's championship, Red Bull's lead decreased from 51 points to 42. Red Bull's lead over Ferrari decreased from 67 to 63.[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-158)
Norris took pole position for the [Dutch Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Dutch_Grand_Prix "2024 Dutch Grand Prix"), ahead of Verstappen, Piastri, Russell, Perez and Leclerc.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-159) At the race start, Verstappen was able to move into the lead from Norris, with Russell moving past Piastri into third and Leclerc moved into fifth. Verstappen was initially able to create a gap to Norris, before Verstappen would complain that "the car doesn't want to turn". Norris was able to close the gap to within a second before executing an overtake on lap 16 before pulling away by several seconds. Leclerc, Russell, Verstappen and Norris all made their pit stops on consecutive laps, with Piastri staying out for longer. When Piastri made his pit stop, the top five were: Norris, Verstappen, Leclerc, Russell and Piastri. Norris continued to extend his lead over Verstappen with Piastri making up ground on Russell, before completing an overtake around the outside of turn one. Piastri proceeded to make up ground on Leclerc, catching him with ten laps to go. Norris took the race win, ahead of Verstappen and Leclerc (who successfully defended third from Piastri).[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-160) With this result, Norris moved to 70 points behind Verstappen, with Leclerc an additional 33 back. In the Constructors's championship, Red Bull moved to 434 points, ahead of McLaren on 404 and Ferrari on 370.[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-161)
At the [Italian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Italian_Grand_Prix "2024 Italian Grand Prix"), Norris and Piastri locked-out the front row for McLaren ahead of Russell and the two Ferraris of Leclerc and Sainz.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-162) Norris was able to maintain his lead at the start, with Piastri following. Russell had to take the escape road at the first corner and damaged his front wing, dropping him to seventh. Russell would make an early pitstop to replace his front wing after a few laps. At the turn 4-5 chicane, Piastri was able to overtake Norris, with Leclerc also making his way past. Norris made his first pit stop on lap 14, and was able to successfully undercut Leclerc, who made his pit stop on the following lap, into second. Piastri was able to maintain the lead following his own pit stop on lap 17. The top three maintained their positions throughout the second stint, with the gaps between them remaining largely stable. Norris made his second pit stop on lap 33, rejoining the race behind Max Verstappen in sixth, Piastri made his pit stop on lap 39, coming back out in fourth, ahead of Verstappen and Norris; Norris made his way past on lap 41, before Verstappen made his second pit stop. On lap 43 of 53, it was Leclerc leading by 11 seconds from Sainz (both drivers running a one-stop stratergy. Piastri closely followed Sainz in third and Norris a few seconds further back in fourth. Lap 45 saw Piastri make his way past Sainz, with Norris making his own way past shortly afterwards. Piastri closed the gap quickly to Leclerc across the closing laps, but was not able to get close enough to attempt an overtake, with Leclerc winning the race ahead of Piastri and Norris, with Championship leader Verstappen in sixth. The race saw the debut of [Franco Colapinto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franco_Colapinto "Franco Colapinto") for Williams, the team replacing [Logan Sargeant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logan_Sargeant "Logan Sargeant") for the rest of the season; Colapinto finished twelfth.[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-163) Following the race, Verstappen's championship lead was cut to 62 points over Norris, Leclerc closed the gap to Norris to 24 points. Red Bull's lead was cut to eight points over McLaren and 39 points over Ferrari.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-164)
### Closing rounds
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2024_Formula_One_World_Championship&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Closing rounds")]
At the [Azerbaijan Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Azerbaijan_Grand_Prix "2024 Azerbaijan Grand Prix"), Leclerc took the pole position ahead of Piastri and Sainz, while Verstappen qualified sixth and Norris down in 17th.[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-165) Norris would start 15th, following the application of penalties for other drivers. In the race, Leclerc maintained his lead off the line with Piastri in second, ahead of Pérez in third. Verstappen made his way into fifth and Norris had moved into 12th by the end of the opening lap. By lap 8 Norris had moved into the points paying positions. Among the leaders, Russell and Verstappen were the first to make pit stops on lap 13, followed by Perez on 14. Piastri, Leclerc and Sainz all pitted soon afterwards. On lap 19, the order was Leclerc, Piastri, Perez, Albon, Norris, Sainz, Verstappen (Albon and Norris had yet to make their first pit stops). Piastri then made a successful move for the lead of the race on the 20th lap and Sainz moved into fourth shortly afterwards. The next laps saw Piastri and Leclerc hold position Perez lose ground to the leading pair and Sainz lose ground to Perez, and Verstappen struggled to get past Norris and Albon - despite having fresher tyres. Norris and Albon would eventually make their pit stops as the lap counter reached the mid to late 30s, with Norris rejoing the race in seventh, behind Verstappen (who had himself lost a position to Russell) Norris would quickly close the gap to Verstappen (courtesy of fresher tyres) and overtake him with two laps to go. Leclerc and Piastri resumed fighting for position on lap 33, allowing Perez and Sainz to rejoing the battle for the lead on laps 42 and 46 respectively. As Leclerc lost tyre performance, Piastri was able to start pulling away, leaving Leclerc to defend second from Perez and Sainz. The battle would continue until Sainz and Perez collided on the penultimate lap, causing both to retire. Piastri therefore took the race win ahead Leclerc, Russell, Norris and Verstappen. Colapinto, who had made his debut in the previous race, scored the first points of his Formula One career, after finishing eighth.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-AZE_F1_race_report-166)[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-167) Following the race's conclusion, Verstappen moved to 313 points ahead of Norris (254) and Leclerc (235). McLaren moved into the lead of the Constructors Championship with 476, leading it for the first time since the [2014 Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Australian_Grand_Prix "2014 Australian Grand Prix"). Red Bull dropped to second, with 456 points, the first time they had not led the Constructors' Championship since the [2022 Miami Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Miami_Grand_Prix "2022 Miami Grand Prix"). Ferrari remained in third, on 425 points.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-AZE_F1_race_report-166)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-168)
Norris took pole at the [Singapore Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Singapore_Grand_Prix "2024 Singapore Grand Prix"), ahead of Verstappen and Hamilton.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-169) At the race start, Norris maintained the lead ahead of Verstappen and Hamilton. Russell and Piastri were fourth and fifth. Norris was able to pull away from Verstappen and Verstappen from Hamilton. Norris would hit the wall, and reported potential front wing damaged, but the team did not make repairs at his pitstop. Across the first phase of pit stops, Norris, Verstappen and Piastri all maintained their positions, but Russell successfully overcut Hamilton into third. Hamilton would subsequently lose fourth to Piastri on track, Piastri making use of fresher tyres - having made his first pit stop 21 laps after Hamilton. Piastri would also overtake Russell. Despite grazing the wall on several occasions, Norris won the race ahead of Verstappen and Piastri with Russell fourth.[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-170) As a result, Norris's deficit to Championship leader Verstappen was reduced to 52 points, Norris lead over third place Leclerc increased to 34 points. In the Constructors's Championship, McLaren's lead increased to 41 points over second placed Red Bull and 75 points over third placed Ferrari.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Formula_One_World_Championship#cite_note-171)
